The prelude is implicitly imported into every module.

## Types

### `Array`

```badger
pub extern type Array<T>
```

Fixed-length immutable contiguous storage.

### `Atom`

```badger
struct Atom<T> { value: T }
```

Shareable synchronized cell: tasks may share one `Atom<T>` (it is
`Transfer` when `T` is), and every operation is indivisible with respect
to other tasks. `update` runs a pure function on the current value.

#### `Atom.compare_and_set`

```badger
fn compare_and_set(self: &Self, expected: T, value: T) -> Bool !{State}
```

Store `value` if the atom still holds `expected`, in one indivisible
step, and say whether it did. `expected` is a value `get` returned:
numbers compare by value, other values by identity (a list equal to
the current one but built separately does not match). `update` is
this in a loop, for a pure `f`.

#### `Atom.get`

```badger
fn get(self: &Self) -> T !{State}
```

#### `Atom.new`

```badger
fn new(value: T) -> Atom<T>
```

#### `Atom.set`

```badger
fn set(self: &Self, value: T) -> Unit !{State}
```

#### `Atom.swap`

```badger
fn swap(self: &Self, value: T) -> T !{State}
```

Store `value` and return the previous value.

#### `Atom.update`

```badger
fn update(self: &Self, f: fn(T) -> T !{}) -> T !{State}
```

Replace the value with `f(value)` and return the new value. `f` may
run again if another task changed the value concurrently.

### `Default`

```badger
protocol Default { default: fn() -> Self }
```

A value to start from: `0`, `0.0`, `false`, `""`, `0s`, an empty
collection, `none`. `derive(Default)` on a struct builds one from each
field's default; `default_of()` gives one where the type is known.

### `HttpStatus`

```badger
protocol HttpStatus { http_code: fn(&Self) -> Symbol, http_status: fn(&Self) -> Int }
```

How an error is reported over HTTP: the status the route system (and
any HTTP server) answers with.

The default is 500 ("internal server error"), so an error type that
says nothing about HTTP keeps the old behaviour. An application
implements it once, on its error type:

```badger
impl HttpStatus for AppError {
    fn http_status(self: &Self) -> Int {
        match self {
            .invalid_input(_) => 400,
            .not_found(_) => 404,
            _ => 500,
        }
    }
}
```

### `OptionMissing`

```badger

```

The error `?` reports on an `Option` that is `none`, in a function
returning `Result<_, E>`: `E` takes it through `From<OptionMissing>`
(a `missing(source: OptionMissing)` variant with `derive(From)`).

### `Seq`

```badger
struct Seq<T, Eff> { pub start: fn() -> fn() -> Option<T> }
```

Typed lazy sequence: a reusable description producing fresh iterators.
`Eff` is what iterating may do (and whether the description captures
task-local state); an iterator itself always stays on its task.

## Functions

### `assert`

```badger
fn assert
```

Terminate the current task with a defect if `condition` is false.

### `default_of`

```badger
fn default_of<T>() -> T where T: Default
```

The default value of the type expected here (`let n: Int = default_of()`).

### `describe_error`

```badger
fn describe_error<E>(e: E) -> String where E: Error
```

The report of an error that ends a program: its code, message, causal
chain, and structured details.

### `diverge`

```badger
fn diverge<T>(never: Never) -> T
```

A value of a block that never finishes, as any type: `let p = e else`
requires its block to leave (`return`, `break`, `continue`, or panic).

### `err`

```badger
fn err<T, E>(error: E) -> Result<T, E>
```

### `error_chain`

```badger
fn error_chain(e: dyn Error) -> List<String>
```

The causal chain of an error, outermost first.

### `hole`

```badger
fn hole<T>() -> T
```

Terminate the current task with a defect.
What `_` in an expression means: a hole, an error reported with the
type expected there (so a partial program checks as far as it can).
